newsitem.title: INDONESIA: No changes in Astra management - paper.
newsitem.headline: No changes in Astra management - paper.

text.p: A group linked to Indonesian President Suharto has said new shareholders in Astra International will not restructure the automobile manufacturer's management team, Bisnis Indonesia newspaper reported on Thursday.
The daily quoted the chairman of the Nusamba group, timber tycoon Muhamad "Bob" Hasan, as saying that Astra had good management and there was no need to bring about any changes.
"However, Astra still needs some improvements. It's just like buying a car, you don't have to change anything. What you need is to tighten the screws," he said.

Nusamba is 80 percent owned by three charitable foundations headed by Suharto. Hasan, a close associate of Suharto and the president's eldest son Sigit Hardjojudanto own 10 percent each. Hasan was quoted as saying Nusamba had bought a 10 percent stake in Astra in recent weeks and had informed the capital markets supervisory agency (Bapepam) of the purchase.
Bapepam officials however said they were yet to receive the letter.
Nusamba is now one of the largest shareholders in the widely-held Astra, in which Toyota Motor Co has an 8.26 percent stake.
Other recent buyers into the company include the Dharamala group with about 7.8 percent and the Salim group with 7.2 percent, newspapers have said.
The Salim group is controlled by Liem Sioe Liong, believed to Indonesia's wealthiest man and a close Suharto associate.
The Dharmala group is controlled by the Gondokusumo family and is one of Indonesia's biggest conglomerates with interests in finance, property and industry.
